task: Analyse how well a CV matches a job description and give specific, actionable improvement recommendations
scoring_calibration: Be strict. Reserve 9-10 only for analyses that a senior recruiter or hiring manager would find genuinely useful — specific, honest, and immediately actionable. Generic advice like 'add more metrics' or 'tailor your CV' with no concrete guidance scores 1-4. Most outputs should score 5-7. An output that inflates the match percentage to make the applicant feel good scores max 4.

dimensions.name: gap_identification
dimensions.description: Does the analysis identify real, specific gaps between the CV and JD — not just obvious surface-level ones? Gaps must reference specific JD requirements that are missing or weak in the CV. Saying 'you lack leadership experience' when the JD mentions 'led cross-functional teams of 10+' scores 8-10. Saying 'you could improve your skills section' with no JD reference scores 1-3.

scoring_guide.1-3: Generic gaps with no JD reference. Could apply to any CV for any job.
scoring_guide.4-6: Identifies some real gaps but misses the most critical ones or lacks JD specificity.
scoring_guide.7-8: Identifies 3+ specific gaps directly tied to JD language and requirements.
scoring_guide.9-10: Identifies all critical gaps with exact JD quotes or requirements. Prioritises gaps by impact on application success.

dimensions.name: actionability
dimensions.description: Does each identified gap come with a specific, concrete fix? 'Add more metrics to your bullets' scores 1-3. 'Rewrite your Practo bullet to mention the 200k patient scale — the JD specifically asks for experience with high-volume consumer products' scores 9-10. Every gap must have a corresponding action.

scoring_guide.1-3: Vague suggestions. 'Tailor your CV to the role', 'highlight relevant experience'.
scoring_guide.4-6: Has suggestions but they're generic — not tied to specific CV bullets or JD requirements.
scoring_guide.7-8: Each gap has a concrete fix that names the specific CV section or bullet to change.
scoring_guide.9-10: Each fix includes: which CV bullet to change, what to add/remove, and why it matters for this specific JD.

dimensions.name: match_score_honesty
dimensions.description: Is the match percentage or rating calibrated and honest? An output that gives 85% match when the CV is clearly missing 3 major JD requirements is dishonest and useless. The score should reflect real alignment — including hard gaps like missing years of experience, required technical skills, or domain experience the CV lacks entirely.

scoring_guide.1-3: Inflated match score. Calls a weak match 'strong' or gives 80%+ with obvious gaps.
scoring_guide.4-6: Match score is in the right ballpark but not calibrated to specific gap severity.
scoring_guide.7-8: Honest match score with clear reasoning tied to specific gaps.
scoring_guide.9-10: Match score is honest, broken down by dimension (e.g. skills: 70%, experience: 50%, domain: 90%), and explains what would move the score up.

dimensions.name: emphasis_guidance
dimensions.description: Does the output tell the applicant which existing CV bullets to move up, reword, or emphasise for this specific JD? Just identifying gaps is not enough — the applicant also needs to know which of their existing strengths to surface more prominently. 'Your Practo bullet about the AI symptom checker should be your first bullet — it directly matches the JD's AI triage requirement' scores 9-10.

scoring_guide.1-3: No guidance on what to emphasise. Only lists what's missing.
scoring_guide.4-6: Vague emphasis guidance — 'highlight your healthcare experience' with no specifics.
scoring_guide.7-8: Names specific CV sections or experiences to move up or expand.
scoring_guide.9-10: Names specific bullets by content, says where to move them and why, tied to specific JD language.
